speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a limp and localized pain, but no fever. To help me understand what might be wrong, could you tell me exactly where the pain is and what activity makes it worse? Also, how long has this been happening?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pain in the knee without fever or trauma is concerning for a referred hip issue in a 7-year-old. Can you pinpoint exactly where the pain is when you press on it, and does it wake him up at night? Also, has he had any recent viral infections or been unusually tired lately? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is highly unusual for a 7-year-old to present with a knee limp and localized pain due to a migraine; those symptoms are classic for hip pathology or transient synovitis. While we await the lab results, please tell me if he has any pain in his groin or buttock, and does he get worse when you straighten his hip against resistance? REQUEST TEST: Anteroposterior Pelvic X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease (Left hip). REQUEST IMAGES: Left hip radiographs to assess for joint space widening or femoral head flattening.
